paragraphs.notes: Continuation of the definition list for R1 in claim 2 ('2. Benzoylcyclohexandione nach Anspruch 1, worin', which opens on printed page 81). The list runs on from the preceding page and this page carries no label of its own for it, so marker is null. The zh field holds the verbatim German: this is a German-language WO publication and there is no Chinese in it. Superscripts and subscripts are printed as true superscripts and subscripts and are transcribed inline: R8, R9, R10, R11, R2, R2a, R13 are printed with raised digits, and the m, n, p in (CH2)m, (CH2)n and (O)p are printed as subscripts, as are the 2 in every CH2 and the 2 in -S-(O). Four terms are broken across a printed line end with a hyphen that is part of the term itself ('3-Tetrahydrothienyl-oxymethyl' and 'Tetrahydropyranyl-oxymethyl'); they are rejoined here as the single printed terms they are. The double space in 'eine der  Gruppen' is as printed and has been kept. Note that 'Tetrahydropyranyl-oxymethyl' appears in the closing 'wobei die Reste' clause among a list of bare ring radicals (Cycloalkyl, Cycloalkenyl, Aryl, Tetrahydrofuranyl, Tetrahydrothienyl, ..., Heteroaryl, Heterocyclyl); read literally it carries the -oxymethyl tail that its neighbours do not. That is what is printed and it has not been normalised. A small stray ink mark sits in the right margin level with the fourth line of this paragraph; it is a scan artifact, not a character.

paragraphs.notes: Definition of R2a inside claim 2. The label R2a is printed flush left with the superscript '2a' on R, then a wide gap before the list; the gap is kept as spaces, matching the layout convention used for the other definition entries in this run. The entry is cut off by the page break: the last printed words are 'Amino, gegebenenfalls substituiertes' and the object of that adjective is on the following page, so the definition is incomplete here and the trailing semicolon is absent. 'Cycloalkenylalkyl' is printed twice in immediate succession on the second line of the entry ('Cycloalkylalkinyl, Cycloalkenylalkyl, Cycloalkenylalkyl, Aryl, ...'). It has been verified at high magnification and it is a genuine duplication in the printed text, not a misread; the surrounding pattern would suggest a 'Cycloalkenylalkenyl' or 'Cycloalkenylalkinyl' was intended, but that is inference and the printed text is left as it stands. Every term in the list is a German-language group name and has been translated in the en field (Halogen- to halo-, -alkinyl to -alkynyl); the initial capitals are German noun capitalisation and are lowercased in the en field.
